sections.h2: Who values and who collects property tax in McCreary County?
sections.html:
McCreary County splits the work between its Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) and its Sheriff. The PVA decides what each parcel is worth, and the Sheriff takes the payment. Because the county has no incorporated city, there is no municipal tax office to add a third stop, and the fiscal court is the only local government setting rates for everyone.

The PVA mails to PO Box 609, Whitley City, KY 42653, and answers at (606) 376-2514, with a fax at (606) 376-4152. The Sheriff's Office is at (606) 376-2322, and the County Clerk, who records deeds and later holds delinquent bills, is at (606) 376-2411. The fiscal court sits at 1 North Main Street in Whitley City and meets on the second Thursday of each month at 6 p.m..

sections.h2: What are the McCreary County tax deadlines?
sections.html:
McCreary County follows the Kentucky calendar in KRS 134.015: the assessment date is January 1, bills are due by December 31, and the Sheriff takes payments until April 15. The cost of paying late climbs in steps.

  • Pay everything by November 1 and you keep 2 percent.
  • From November 2 to December 31, the printed amount is due.
  • January adds 5 percent.
  • After January 31 the add-on becomes 10 percent.

In 2026 the discount deadline of November 1 has gone by, so the remaining 2026 choices are the printed amount through December 31 or a penalty after that. Bills still open after April 15 go to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency. The county attorney then mails two notices, and the Clerk must schedule a sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer. A buyer at that sale can add its own fees, so it pays to clear the balance with the Sheriff first.

sections.h2: How much tax does a McCreary County house carry?
sections.html:
Less than almost anywhere else in Kentucky, because home values are low. The Census Bureau puts the median owner-occupied value at $85,300, against $188,100 in McCracken County. The state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100 turns that median into about $90.42 of state tax. County, school and any district rates are added by the local bodies, and the PVA can tell you the combined figure for a given address.

With no permits issued in 2025, new construction is not adding much to the tax roll. That leaves existing houses as the market. The 2020 census counted 6,892 housing units in the county, and 12.1 percent of them stood vacant. Another 17.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, which is the group the homestead exemption is written for, and Census figures list 785 veterans in the county.

sections.h2: Who can claim the homestead exemption in McCreary County?
sections.html:
Homeowners aged 65 or older, and owners classed as totally disabled, can claim a deduction of $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. The Department of Revenue applies it to the assessed value, then figures the tax on what remains.

The effect is large here. A house valued at the county median of $85,300 would be taxed on only $36,200, and the state share falls from about $90.42 to about $38.37. File at the PVA office in Whitley City, bringing a birth certificate, driver's license or passport as proof of age. A disability claim must rest on a federal or retirement-system finding of total disability, and it is renewed yearly unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or has been judged totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: How does a McCreary County owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
The first move is a conference with the PVA or a deputy, who is required to explain how the value was reached. Without it, no appeal can be filed. The statutory sequence runs like this:

  • The real property roll is open to the public for 13 days starting the first Monday in May.
  • After the conference, the owner files the appeal with the County Clerk by the close of business on the day following the last inspection day.
  • The local board of assessment appeals sits 25 to 35 days after inspection closes and hears evidence only with the PVA and the owner or representative present.
  • Evidence should cover the land and structures, insurance, building costs and comparable sales. Appeals lacking documents are denied.

Skipping the board hearing ends the right to carry the case to the Kentucky Claims Commission. If the board sets a value above your claim after bills are printed, you get a supplemental bill for the gap. Photographs, a survey and comparable sales help support the value of a rural tract.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid McCreary County taxes at a sale?
sections.html:
The debt does not disappear. Under KRS 134.015, taxes are the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and the lien under KRS 134.420 lasts up to 11 years whoever holds title. Once the Clerk has the bill, interest runs at 1 percent a month and commissions for the Clerk and county attorney are added, plus a fee to record and release the lien.

Closing agents usually require the payoff. Call the Sheriff before April 15 for the current balance, and call the Clerk afterward.

sections.h2: What is McCreary County, Kentucky, like for a seller?
sections.html:
McCreary is the youngest and last-formed of Kentucky's 120 counties, carved in 1912 from parts of Pulaski, Wayne and Whitley. It covers 431 square miles on the western edge of the Cumberland Plateau and is the only Kentucky county with no incorporated city. Whitley City is the seat, and Pine Knot and Stearns are the other census-designated places. About 43 percent of the county lies in the Daniel Boone National Forest and 18 percent in the Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area, so privately owned land is a modest share of the whole.

Timber, coal and the Cincinnati Southern Railway, which reached the county in 1880, shaped its early economy, and the Stearns company town grew from that history. Cumberland Falls State Park and the Big South Fork Scenic Railway now bring visitors. Students attend the McCreary County School District, whose main high school is McCreary Central. The county keeps Eastern time, and the Census counts 17,124 residents in 2025, up 1.4 percent from 2020.

Workers spend a mean 32.3 minutes getting to their jobs, and 80.1 percent of households have broadband. Neighbors include Pulaski, Laurel, Whitley and Wayne counties, plus two in Tennessee. For an owner who inherited a house here or fell behind on tax, an as-is cash sale can close without repair work.

faqs.q: Does McCreary County have a city tax in addition to the county tax?
faqs.a: No. McCreary is the only Kentucky county with no incorporated city, so county government is the single local government. School and district levies still appear on the bill.

faqs.q: Where do I pay McCreary County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the McCreary County Sheriff, reachable at (606) 376-2322, through April 15. The PVA at (606) 376-2514 values property but does not take payments.

faqs.q: What is the state share of tax on a $85,300 McCreary County home?
faqs.a: About $90.42, using the 2025 state rate of 10.6 cents per $100. Local levies come on top of that figure.

faqs.q: Can a 65-year-old McCreary County owner cut the tax base?
faqs.a: Yes. The homestead exemption removes $49,100 from the assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the PVA office with proof of age.

faqs.q: What if my McCreary County tax bill goes to the County Clerk?
faqs.a: After April 15 it becomes a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien. Interest of 1 percent a month accrues, and a sale to an investor can follow 90 to 135 days after the transfer.
